nodes.characterization_summary: CV clearly resolved two, or even three distinguishable H chemisorption states at Pt(poly), dependent on co-adsorption of anions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: However, cyclic voltammetry work, later [8], clearly resolved two, or even three distinguisable H chemisorption states at Pt(poly), dependent on co-adsorption of anions [9,10].

nodes.characterization_summary: Impedance spectroscopy results for Pt(100) in aq. H₂SO₄ show competitive chemisorption between HSO₄⁻ and H.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Somewhat similar, but smaller, competitive chemisorption between HSO₄⁻ and H arises at the (100) surface as indicated by impedance spectroscopy results obtained by Morin, Barber and Conway [18], illustrated in Fig. 2, compared with a normalized cyclic voltammogram.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cyclic voltammograms for Pt(111) show charge response region of ca. 33% due to HSO₄⁻ chemisorption in distinction from UPD H.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The latter procedure has enabled the CV profile at Pt(111) in aq. H₂SO₄, over the potential range 0.05-0.35 V, to be resolved into two components: one due to UPD of H... and the remaining 1/3 associated with chemisorption of HSO₄⁻ ion (Fig. 1)...

nodes.characterization_summary: OPD H pseudocapacitance profiles and coverages during HER at Ni-Mo alloys approach constant limiting values <1 with increasing overpotential.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Results are shown in Figs. 8 and 9 for H OPD capacitance and coverage as a function of η for the HER at three single-phase Ni-/Mo alloy cathodes, data being derived from potential-relaxation transients [57].

nodes.characterization_summary: IR band at 2090 cm⁻¹ assigned to atop H-metal vibration at Pt, Rh, Ir, and Pt(111) near H₂ reversible potential.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Later work by Bewick with Nichol [65,66], on H absorption at polycrystalline Pt, Rh and Ir, and Pt(111) in aq. H₂SO₄ up to 1 M concentration confirmed... At the potential for onset of the process, an IR-adsorption band arose at 2090 cm⁻¹ which was assigned to atop H-metal vibration...

nodes.characterization_summary: Complex-plane impedance plots for HER at Pt(hkl) surfaces in 0.5 M aq. H₂SO₄ show sensitivity to 2-d surface structure with reactivity order (100)sII < (111) < (110).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 11 shows how the complex-plane plots depend appreciably on the index of the Pt crystal face... The order of reactivity increases from (100)sII to (110), parallel to the increasing dominance of the H₂ diffusion effect.

nodes.characterization_summary: Temperature-dependent CV (0-80°C) on Pt(100), (110), (111) surfaces enabled determination of heats of adsorption of H decreasing in order (100) > (111) > (110), decreasing by 50-60% with H coverage from 5 to 80%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Temperature effects (0-80°C) were studied... on the three principal-index planes... The enthalpies of electro-chemisorption of H were found to decrease in the order (100) > (111) > (110), except for H coverages >80%. Generally, the heats of adsorption decreased appreciably, by 50-60%, with increase of H coverage from 5 to 80%.
